plan.name: Deferred follow-ups (issues from specs 12-35)
plan.conventions: These packages close FOLLOW-UP ISSUES, not specs, so the issue body is the contract and there is no spec file to check against. Read the whole issue first and account for EVERY numbered item in the PR body, as a table with one row per item and a verdict: fixed, already resolved on main (name the commit), or not fixed and why. Verify each item against current main BEFORE changing anything - these issues were filed across five weeks of shipping and later waves fixed some of them in passing, so report an item that is already correct instead of re-fixing correct code. Do not widen scope to neighbouring code: an item you believe is wrong gets an argument in the PR, not a silent extra change. The COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME derived from this repo directory is sanitized before it reaches a worktree's .env (#115, fixed on main before this plan started), so a plain docker compose call in a package worktree needs no workaround; the orchestrator also runs docker compose down -v --remove-orphans in a package's own worktree the moment its issue closes, so a finished package's stack does not linger into the next one - this never touches docker-compose.e2e.yml (that file needs an explicit -f, which this call does not pass). Whether an E2E stack itself is safely isolated per worktree is still open (#190) - never bring the E2E stack up while another session might be using it; inside a sequential wave that is automatic. e2e/fixtures/seed.sql is this plan's hottest collective file and the rule is NOT one storage per package - read that file's own comments before adding anything. Adding NEW rows to the shared E2E Household storage is correct and is exactly what e2e/specs/products.spec.js already does, one product per scenario, because it logs in as e2e-bob whose only membership is that storage; a package extending an existing spec file follows that file's established pattern with its own product and batch ids taken from the next free range. What must never happen is mutating a row another scenario reads, or writing DURABLE per-user state of a shared user - e2e-alice and e2e-bob above all, whose start_page and barcode_prompt_seen_at other spec files assert on while the suite runs fully parallel. A package that must write durable user state gets its own dedicated user and storage, the way e2e-start, e2e-inbox and e2e-stocktake do. Keep ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING and pick a genuinely unused id: a colliding id is dropped in silence and the test then passes against somebody else's row. internal/httpapi/router.go is append-only and no package in this plan should need a new route. Apply the silent invariants from CLAUDE.md throughout: 404-not-403 for unknown AND inaccessible storages and for the whole admin area, with an identical response either way; is_admin re-queried from the DB on every admin request, never returned in any JSON and never a client-side branch; debug_reason only when APP_ENV is dev, emitted from the single error serializer; same-storage validation on every id - path, parent_id, move target, confirm-body field; every inventory_batches write paired, in the same transaction, with an inventory_logs row; EXIF stripped from every upload with orientation applied to pixels FIRST; expiry cascades touching derived dates only, never user ones. Every build, test and migration runs through docker compose - no host toolchain, per docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md. Any package that adds or renames a file under web/static/ belonging to the cached app shell adds it to SHELL_ASSETS in web/static/sw.js and bumps CACHE_VERSION; on a conflict on that one line, keep the higher version and both additions. Every new user-visible string goes through spec 19's catalogs, with the key in both en.json and de.json. Never add a storage_members row for a shared fixture user (e2e-alice, e2e-bob) even temporarily - a second membership changes what the storage switcher does and breaks e2e/specs/storage-switching.spec.js, which is the same class of durable shared state as start_page and barcode_prompt_seen_at above. When writing a consolidation PR body, never put a closing keyword (close, closes, fix, fixes, resolve, resolves, and their past tenses) immediately before a # reference to the wave issue - not even in prose describing the manual close, since GitHub auto-closes on that pattern anywhere in the body; write it as the wave issue is closed by hand afterwards (#NNN) instead, and before opening the PR run gh pr view <PR> --json closingIssuesReferences and reword the body if the wave issue's own number appears there. Before treating a red E2E suite as a finding, reset it: docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml down -v, then build, run --rm app migrate up, up -d, and reseed (MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 on Windows) before running the suite again - a stack that already ran once reports failures that are not real and that grow run over run as seeded rows accumulate, so a red suite is never a blocking finding until it has been re-run on a freshly reset stack, and the consolidator should leave the stack reset and reseeded but not yet run so review-tests' own bare run --rm e2e passes clean rather than burning a review round on a dirty stack.

packages.focus: Work the numbered items of #140: 1 to 4 are script behaviour, 5 to 9 are test gaps, 10 to 14 are documentation. Item 1 (-Wave together with -Slug passing the finished-wave guard on the wrong wave's closed issue) and item 2 (the shared inventory-e2e project having no foreignDir veto on the working_dir rule) are the two that can remove something they should not - do those first and prove each with a case in scripts/tests/wellen-docker-cleanup.test.ps1. The orchestrator may be running against THIS plan while you work: it re-reads wellen-docker-cleanup.ps1 at every call but reads wellen-orchestrator.ps1 only once at start, so your changes must stay backward-compatible with a wave file and an orchestrator you did not write and must not require a new field. Wave 1 is deliberately marked dockerCleanup false so your rewrite is never used to clean the wave that produced it - do not change that flag. #115 is no longer a package of this wave: it was fixed on main before this wave started (Get-SanitizedProjectName in scripts/wellen-orchestrator.ps1, with a committed test in scripts/tests/wellen-orchestrator.test.ps1), together with a new Stop-PackageStack function that runs `docker compose down -v --remove-orphans` in a package's own worktree the moment its issue closes - read both before touching that file. Item 9 (untested orchestrator paths: the Invoke-WaveDockerCleanup job wrapper, the -Validate check, the -Wave plus CLOSED path) and item 14 (a stale claim that closed waves are skipped "regardless" of dockerCleanup) both name wellen-orchestrator.ps1 lines that have since moved and, for item 9, a file that now has its own test alongside wellen-docker-cleanup.test.ps1 - verify both against current main and its line numbers rather than the issue's, which predate this fix. Items 12 and 13 touch scripts/wellen-planen.md, and item 13's one-off wave-3 instruction is stale now that the Extended-core plan is complete - remove it rather than rewording it. Never run a docker system, volume, network or image prune, and do not remove Docker resources by hand outside the script under test.

Work the numbered items of #124; items 1 to 4 are real bugs in deploy/synology/update and come first. Item 1 is the dangerous one: the old container id is read before a pull and build that can take minutes and is never re-read, so an EXIT trap firing after the app was recreated in that gap removes the LIVE app container - re-read app_ids just before arming the trap and refuse if it changed. Item 2 is the same family: app_ids_all lacks the compose oneoff False label filter, so the trap can force-remove a concurrent one-off docker compose run container, and the pre-flight calls an orphaned migrate up container a stopped app container. Item 4 (a removed new instance leaving its accepted jobs pending) is NOT yours to fix - it belongs to #121 in wave 4, so record in the PR what you leave to it. This script runs unattended on the operator's NAS against a live stack, so a change that merely looks right is not enough: state for each item how you convinced yourself, and where you could not (DSM busybox, standalone Compose, the containerd image store) say so plainly rather than implying you tested it. The documentation items touch deploy/synology/README.md and docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md, which #112 also edits later in this wave - keep to the sections the issue names. Do not add a rollback path or a new flag nobody asked for.

Work the numbered items of #112. Item 2 is very likely already resolved: it asks for a caveat naming #111 while #111 is open, and #111 (spec 30, the setup wizard) shipped in wave 1 of plan #97 - verify against main, and if the wizard no longer writes a commented-out STATIC_DIR then report the item as resolved and add no caveat. Item 1 is a Go change in internal/config/config.go and internal/config/setup.go: the missing-.env error and the wizard's closing hint both print a bare docker compose up -d with no -f, which on the NAS variant loads the dev override and starts Traefik on DSM's own port 80 - either stop printing a compose invocation or make it overridable, and do not reintroduce the inline-comment format that spec 30 deliberately removed from .env.example. Items 3 and 4 and the nits are documentation across README.md, migrations/README.md, docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md, docs/specs/02-data-model.md, docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.nas.yml; #124 runs earlier in this wave and also edits deploy/synology/README.md and spec 01, so read what it left. The .gitattributes item matters more than it looks: the host has core.autocrlf true and a CRLF shebang would break deploy/synology/compose on the NAS. Nothing here changes what runs except item 1.

Decide the question in #128 repo-wide and implement the decision in internal/httpapi/errors.go ALONE - the change belongs inside Internal(), not swept across its call sites, and #131 is editing another file in the same package in parallel. Either populate the failure's Reason from the wrapped error so a 500 carries debug_reason in dev like every other status, or document on Internal() why an internal error's text is the one category never shown to a client even in dev. This sits directly on a silent invariant from CLAUDE.md: debug_reason only when APP_ENV is dev, emitted from the single error serializer. Whichever way you decide, the gate and the single-serializer rule must come out untouched, and a test must pin that a 500 carries no debug_reason when APP_ENV is not dev - that test is required even on the document-it-and-change-nothing branch, because it is what stops the next reviewer re-raising this. The reviewer who filed it verified that nothing leaks today, so do not treat this as a leak fix. Do not change any handler, do not add a new error constructor, and do not touch router.go.

internal/vision/live_test.go's TestLiveAnalyzeProductHonoursContract runs whenever the local .env holds a real GEMINI_API_KEY and fails the whole suite when Gemini answers 503 or 429. Make a provider outage skip the test while keeping a contract violation inside a SUCCESSFUL response a hard failure - that distinction is the entire point, so a blanket skip on any error is the wrong fix. CI is unaffected either way because it sets no key, and this project's own sessions blank the key deliberately (docker compose run --rm -e GEMINI_API_KEY= app go test ./...), so this is a test almost nobody watches fail: say in the PR how you exercised both branches without waiting for a real outage. That is the whole issue - one test file, no production code in internal/vision, no new dependency, and no retry loop.

Two items from #131, both small and both already scoped by the issue. Item 1: internal/store/notifications_test.go exercises the upper send_hour boundary but not a negative value - add a case asserting a negative send_hour is rejected with ErrValidation, and if the API layer has its own range check, a 422 carrying send_hour in fields. Item 2: docs/specs/17-expiry-notifications.md does not document the test endpoint answering 409 while enabled is FALSE (the no-code-path-can-send criterion covers the test button too) or 404 for an unknown or inaccessible storage - add both to the spec's API section in that section's existing shape. The 404 there is the usual invariant: unknown and inaccessible must be indistinguishable, so document one response and not two. #128 is editing internal/httpapi/errors.go in parallel, so keep to the notification-settings handler and its test. A stored delivery token must still never be returned by any read - do not add one to a response while documenting the endpoint.

packages.spec: Issue 133: backup and restore round trip
packages.focus: Build the restore round trip #133 describes as an E2E-level job in e2e/, run by .github/workflows/e2e.yml - the deployment gate rather than a PR gate, so the cost lands where that workflow's own header and spec 01 say it belongs. The sequence is: bring the stack up, migrate, seed, run scripts/backup (an executable file at exactly that path), tear the stack down INCLUDING its volumes, bring it back up, restore from the artifact, then assert that /healthz answers 200 AND that the data actually came back. Asserting only the 200 is the failure mode to avoid, and so is the weaker version of it - one product rendering on one page - because a restore that silently dropped every inventory_logs row, every admin_audit_log row, or the whole of a second storage would pass both. Pin it concretely: capture per-table row counts BEFORE the teardown and compare them after the restore, covering at minimum products, inventory_batches, inventory_logs, locations, categories, storages, storage_members, users, jobs and admin_audit_log, then additionally assert the field values of at least one specific row per storage for more than one storage, so a restore that keeps the counts but scrambles the contents also fails. A test whose assertion cannot distinguish a good restore from a lossy one is the one outcome this package must not produce. That volume destruction is why this package runs alone in its own wave - docker-compose.e2e.yml pins one Compose project name for every worktree, so it would take a concurrent session's stack with it. The gap is load-bearing now: docs/specs/18-operations-and-observability.md names restoring the pre-upgrade backup as the ONLY rollback, with no migrate down in production, so this is the first time that path is ever executed end to end. Per docs/specs/15-backup-restore-and-export.md the archive deliberately excludes imagecache and .env - a restore that expects either is testing the wrong contract. No host toolchain: every step goes through docker compose. Do not change what scripts/backup produces; if the round trip shows the format is wrong, report that rather than redesigning it here.

Decide #121 explicitly between its two shapes and say which in the PR. Shape A records which process owns a pending job (a column, or a lease with a heartbeat) and fails only jobs whose owner is gone - if you take it, the migration is migrations/00014_job_lease.sql and NO OTHER NUMBER, with a down block that internal/migrate's rollback test actually reaches. Shape B fails only pending jobs older than the runner's DefaultTimeout - no migration, and 00014 stays unused for a later plan. Store.FailInterruptedJobs in internal/store/jobs.go today marks EVERY pending row failed at start-up, and its own comment states the single-process assumption that the NAS rolling update in deploy/synology/update breaks on purpose. Read #124 item 4 as part of this: the update script's trap force-removes a new instance and the jobs it had accepted stay pending with nothing sweeping them, which is the same defect seen from the other end. Whatever you choose must keep the stop-then-start case working exactly as it does now - a job whose process really did die must still be failed, or a crash leaves work stuck pending forever - and must not make Recover slow enough to delay the listener. Do not change the job runner's timeout semantics and do not add a second runner.

internal/store/users.go, storages.go and catalog.go each re-check RowsAffected after their delete and return ErrNotFound rather than recording an admin_audit_log row for a deletion the request did not perform, and that branch has no test - the existing delete-a-missing-X cases reach the earlier pgx.ErrNoRows branch on the name lookup instead, so the re-check could be deleted and the suite would stay green. #139 offers two honest outcomes and BOTH are acceptable: build a small two-connection helper in internal/store that interleaves two transactions deterministically and test the branch with it, or decide the branch is defensive, leave it, and say so in a comment at all three sites explaining why no test here can reach it. Choose deliberately and argue it in the PR - the one outcome this issue exists to prevent is the branch staying both untested and unexplained. If you build the helper it is the wave's shared one: #136 runs after you and needs the same kind of isolation, so make it general enough to reuse and say in the PR what it does and does not give. Every audit row still pairs with its deletion in one transaction per docs/specs/18-operations-and-observability.md - do not split them to make testing easier.

Two tests in internal/store/delta_test.go fail intermittently under full-suite load, both with the same symptom: the watermark comes back earlier than the test's own cursor. The cause is understood and written up in #136 - deltaWatermark takes the least of now() and min(xact_start) across the whole database, so a transaction another package holds open drags it backwards. DO NOT LOOSEN deltaWatermark: that rule is correct and deliberate, and a real client simply gets a slightly older cursor and re-receives a row, which the at-least-once contract in docs/specs/12-client-api-contract.md already allows. This is a test-isolation problem only. Fix it either by making the two assertions tolerant of a watermark that legitimately lags, or by giving these two tests a database nothing else is touching - #139 runs before you in this wave and may already have left a helper for exactly that, so read what it built rather than writing a second one. Demonstrate the fix rather than asserting it: the issue records one failure in six full-suite runs, so a single green run proves nothing - say in the PR how you convinced yourself, for instance by reproducing the failure first against a deliberately held-open transaction.

Work the numbered items of #154. Items 1 and 2 are web/static/js/tree-modal.js and matter most: the backdrop test comparing the event target to the dialog is also true for a click on the dialog's own padding, because .card puts its padding on the dialog element, so a misclick loses a typed and unsubmitted root name; and close() does not wait for an in-flight create POST, so createdIds can resolve without it, the caller's refresh GET races the commit, and a late error lands in a dialog that is already gone. #144 runs immediately after you in this wave and adds a shared already-open guard to the same file - leave it in a shape that guard can sit on, and do not pre-empt it. Items 4 to 6 are stale documentation: specs 26 and 27 say js/review.js renders the fields and holds the trigger call site when the real call sites are openLocationField in web/static/js/location-options.js and openCategoryField in web/static/js/category-options.js, and location-options.js's own header still claims it is only for spec 06's upload and review screens. Item 6 (spec 28's three review screens wording) was handed to #145 in plan #97 - check main first and report it as already resolved if it is. Item 3 is a nit in web/static/js/pages/review.js and item 7 a fixture-comment mismatch. None of this changes a backend endpoint or any silent invariant: if you find yourself editing Go, stop and explain why in the PR.

Put a single already-open guard inside openTreeManager in web/static/js/tree-modal.js so a second call of either kind is refused while one dialog is open. That is the fix #144 asks for and the only one that actually covers the case: js/location-options.js's openLocationField and js/category-options.js's openCategoryField each disable only their own trigger and neither knows about the other kind, so more per-trigger disabling in the callers would not help. #154 runs immediately before you in this wave and changes the same file's backdrop handling and close() - build on what it left rather than reverting it. Decide refuse-or-queue deliberately and say which in the PR; refusing is simpler and nothing in the specs asks for queueing. Add the e2e coverage the issue notes is missing: open a location field's trigger, then a category field's trigger on the same screen, and assert exactly one dialog exists on document.body. Both dialogs are independently scoped to their own kind and storageId today, so nothing is silently wrong and no CLAUDE.md invariant is at risk - this is a stacked-dialog UI fix, and it must not change the behaviour of either quick-create path.

Guard the split and move submit handlers in web/static/js/pages/products.js against a double-click racing the in-flight request, following the pattern already present in this file's own import: openLocationField in js/location-options.js disables the trigger and clears it in a finally. Two quick clicks on Split can each pass the server's per-request validation and stack silently - splitting 2 off a batch of 5 twice legally succeeds both times, leaving the source at 1 and two new batches instead of one, with no error shown. FIRST verify the premise the reviewer could not: #161 records that the race was read from internal/httpapi/batches.go only, not from internal/store/batches.go's actual transaction and row-locking behaviour, so read the store and say in the PR whether the race is reachable before deciding the fix. The endpoints stay authoritative and untouched - same-storage validation of target_location_id and location_id stays server-side, every write still pairs with its inventory_logs row, and a client-side upper-bound check is NOT the fix. Items 2 and 3 are nits: an invalid submit silently no-ops with no feedback, and parseInt truncates 2.5 to 2 and sends a different number than the field shows. #135 in wave 8 refactors this same file, so keep your edit confined to the two submit handlers.

Three items from #174. Item 1 is the only behaviour change: in web/static/js/pages/stocktake.js, confirm() calls showNotice() unconditionally after reload(), which stomps the message reload() sets on both of its failure branches - so a housemate deleting the location between the successful POST and the reload GET leaves the user with a bare success notice and no sign the location is gone. The file already has the right shape in reloadKeepingError(), used by the 422 path; give the success path an equivalent rather than inventing a third pattern. Item 2 is an e2e gap: locationPathFor in web/static/js/pages/products.js joins a location path with a separator, and every existing assertion including this feature's own fixture uses a single-segment root location, so add a batch at least two levels deep and assert the full path and its order. Item 3 is the chooser's zero-locations empty state, implemented in renderChooser and the chooser-empty element but covered by no test. In item 1's scenario the write has already committed, so nothing is corrupted and no CLAUDE.md invariant is involved - do not change the confirm endpoint or spec 13's exact-row-set semantics. #166 in wave 6 adds another test to this page's suite afterwards, so leave e2e/specs/stocktake.spec.js easy to extend.

Add the assertion #157 asks for and change no production code: web/static/js/barcode-offer.js already calls hasBarcodeAlready() before shouldOffer(), which is correct, and the issue exists because nothing pins it. Swapping the two lines would make a product that already carries a barcode consume the user's one-time explanatory copy without the offer ever being shown, because shouldOffer() posts to the prompt-shown route and burns users.barcode_prompt_seen_at unconditionally - and the existing test asserting that a product with a barcode is never offered another passes in BOTH orders, because no dialog appears either way. So assert the side effect rather than the absence of a dialog: that barcode_prompt_seen_at, or the first_time flag derived from it, is unaffected by an offerBarcodeCapture call against a product that already has a code. It needs a user whose seen_at is still NULL, so give it its own fixture user - do not reuse e2e-dana, whose state the rest of that spec file moves around. The sentence you are pinning is docs/specs/20-barcode-recall.md's criterion that barcode_prompt_seen_at is set exactly once, on the first time the offer is SHOWN. If you find yourself editing barcode-offer.js, you have misread the issue.

Add one e2e test and no production change: #166 is a coverage gap on a fix that is already in place and already verified by a reviewer. renderFound's found-on-shelf list in web/static/js/pages/stocktake.js formats a bare date from the found-item form's date input and carries the UTC timeZone option that stops Intl.DateTimeFormat rendering it a day early for any viewer west of UTC; its sibling call site in renderRow has a regression test, this one does not. Drive the found-on-shelf form under a non-UTC browser timezone - the timezoneId option on test.use is the pattern e2e/specs/localization.spec.js already establishes - add an item with a known expiry date, and assert the rendered list item shows that calendar date and not the day before. #169 runs after you and extends the same localization spec file, and #174 in wave 5 has already changed stocktake.js and its spec file, so read what both left. Do not re-fix the timezone bug and do not disturb the other call site's existing test.

packages.spec: Issue 169: audited German relative time test
packages.focus: Add one e2e assertion and no production change. web/static/js/audited.js switched Intl.RelativeTimeFormat from the browser default locale to getLanguage(), the resolved app language - a real behaviour change shipped in the same PR that introduced getLanguage(), so neither side of that pair is pinned by a test. Assert under a de override that the audited relative-time label renders the German phrase rather than the English one; e2e/specs/localization.spec.js already establishes the override pattern, and the location audit timestamp on locations.html is the natural surface. #166 runs immediately before you and extends the same spec file, so read what it left rather than restructuring it. This is display-only with no data and no security impact - a regression would show an English relative-time phrase inside an otherwise German UI. Do not change audited.js, and do not add catalog keys for a string Intl generates.

Add the missing cancel test in e2e/specs/products.spec.js and change no production code. The cancel criterion in docs/specs/28-batch-move-quick-create.md names both forms - cancelling the modal by Esc or backdrop leaves the in-progress split OR move form untouched - but the only cancel test opens the split toggle and scopes entirely to the split form. splitLocationAdd and moveLocationAdd in web/static/js/pages/products.js are two independent closures with their own openedSelect, which is exactly why an earlier round found the move form's completion path untested; the same independence leaves its cancel wiring unverified. Mirror the existing split-picker cancel test against the move form's own trigger and assert its quantity-independent state, the selected location, survives both an Esc and a real backdrop click. Assert with non-default values: a placeholder-versus-placeholder comparison cannot fail. Follow the file's one-product-per-scenario convention with a dedicated product and batch, or establish that the existing move-picker fixture can be reused without racing the completion test in the same file - say which in the PR. #161 in wave 5 has already touched these two handlers, so read what it left.

Two documentation fixes from #168. First, the File layout tree in docs/specs/05-frontend-pwa-foundations.md lists every other shared js/ module, including js/nav.js for a spec that had not landed when it was written, but has no entry for js/i18n.js and no i18n/ directory for en.json and de.json - add both, and add an Amended by 19-localization.md note in the same style as the existing Amended by notes for specs 29 and 34. That module is foundational: its own header says every page imports it before rendering anything of its own, so a maintainer scanning this section to learn which shared modules exist currently will not find it. Second, achievementLabel in web/static/js/gamification.js points at this module's localization report, which exists nowhere in the repo - the substantive statement is correct, that no gamification achievement catalog keys are translated yet so labels fall back to snake_case, so remove or replace the dangling pointer and keep the reason. Documentation accuracy only: no runtime behaviour, no test, no catalog key. Do not add the missing achievement keys - that is spec 51 and 52 work and belongs to a later phase.

Fold the round-1 review findings in #130 into docs/spikes/31-on-device-expiry-reminders.md. This REVISES a spike, it does not promote or implement one: docs/spikes/ is explicitly not a contract per CLAUDE.md, a spike becomes work only by being promoted into a numbered spec first, and nothing on-device is being built here. The substantive corrections are the overstated absolutes (the wrapper does have a push handler calling showNotification and a notificationclick handler, so it is wrong to say it has no local-notification code; and the claim that the PWA has no way to run while nobody has it open is stated as fact while not appearing in Not verified), the CACHE_VERSION rule attributed to spec 05 when the constant lives in web/static/sw.js, and the proposed server-side bucket endpoint conflicting with spec 08, which defines urgency as computed client-side. The security and privacy argument needs the gaps the issue lists: a removed member's leftover badge, shown notification and periodicsync registration; what a background fetch does with an expired session; a notification body pinned to counts only, because spec 17's digest lines carry product name, quantity and location and those show on a lock screen; and where a per-user, per-device setting would live, given a service worker cannot read the localStorage that holds the active storage. Give gate 1 a pass-fail threshold and named OS and browser versions so it can actually fail, and move the spec 17 decision out of this spike's own acceptance gates. The reviewers had no web access, so anything checked only against pages fetched while writing the spike belongs in Not verified - including the iOS finding about spec 17, which is the spike's headline claim about an accepted spec.

Lift the suggestion picker out of web/static/js/review.js into a module both it and web/static/js/pages/products.js import, and wire the product detail view's two picture-change paths, suggestion picker and custom upload, onto the routes that already exist. NO NEW BACKEND: the image PATCH route taking a suggestion hash or an icon_name, and the image-suggestions GET, are both wired and tested and are simply unreachable from the product page today, so internal/httpapi/router.go must come out untouched. This is the only package in the plan that adds a feature, and it runs alone and last because the picker's current callers are three review screens - the refactor must leave their behaviour identical, their existing e2e journeys are the evidence, so run them and say so in the PR. docs/specs/16-product-maintenance.md already describes the detail view as showing the image with the change paths from spec 07, so the spec needs no new criterion; it needs the page to match what it already says. Same-storage validation and the identical 404 for an unknown and an inaccessible storage stay with the existing handlers - do not reimplement either client-side - and EXIF stripping with orientation applied to pixels first stays in the upload path you are reusing, not reimplemented here. The new module goes into SHELL_ASSETS in web/static/sw.js with a CACHE_VERSION bump, and every new string goes through spec 19's catalogs in both en.json and de.json.

Work three issues in internal/httpapi/errors.go and its test file, closing all of #202, #203 and #204 in one PR body table. #202: FromStoreError's resync branch puts err.Error() straight into Reason for store.ErrResyncRequired, which is safe today only because that sentinel has exactly one return site (internal/store/delta.go:222) and exactly one caller of ResyncRequired - but errors.Is matches through wrapping, so a future delta path that wraps the sentinel with fmt.Errorf would leak its own wrapping text as debug_reason with nothing failing. Either pin it with a test asserting the exact Reason string (spec 12 only specifies the 409 resync_required status and code, not this dev-only text, so there is no spec reason to preserve the current wording - just no reason to change it gratuitously either), or remove the dependence by using the sentinel's own fixed text or a named Reason... constant instead of err.Error() - the smaller surface and matches how every other Reason in the package is produced. Either way needs a test - the current state has neither, and that is the actual gap, not just the source of the string. #203: add a test asserting an UpstreamFailed response carries only code and message (no debug_reason) in both dev and non-dev, decoding the envelope and checking key presence rather than substring-matching, the same pattern TestInternalCarriesNoDebugReason already uses; and extend or add a case to the FromStoreError table asserting its default branch (a second producer of a 500 alongside direct Internal() calls) also carries no debug_reason and no trace of the error's text. #204: the Reason... const block's header comment claims spec 03 names all of these values, but ReasonNoRouteMatch and ReasonMethodNotAllowed are the router's own refusals and appear in no spec - either fix the comment to say the first six are spec 03's and the router's two are this package's own, or bring spec 03's Defined values list into line with the code (deciding this deliberately: spec 03's section is specifically about authorization failures, and the router's two refusals are not authorization outcomes, so fixing the comment is likely the right shape). This sits directly on CLAUDE.md's debug_reason silent invariant - every new test must exercise both APP_ENV=dev and non-dev. Do not add a new error constructor, do not change any handler, and do not touch router.go.

internal/store/export_test.go's TestExportStorageCarriesNoCredentialMaterial derives its admin username from the first eight hex characters of a UUIDv7 storage id (export_test.go:112), and a truncated UUIDv7 is a timestamp, not a nonce - the leading 48 bits change only once every 2^16 ms (about 65.5 seconds), so two runs inside the same window mint the same username and CreateUser correctly rejects the duplicate, making go test -count=2 ./internal/store/ red on a clean tree. Fix it the way every other test in the package already does: Username: admin- + randomSuffix() (the helper used throughout auth_test.go, bootstrap_test.go, catalog_test.go, clientsync_test.go and more), not a slice of the storage id. While in the file, grep -rn String()[:8] internal/store/*_test.go for any other test with the same bug - testdb_test.go's newStorage does the identical thing for storages.name (testdb_test.go:208), harmless today only because that column has no unique constraint; fix it too if you touch that helper, or say explicitly why you left it. No production code changes, no behaviour change - this is a test's own value generation only. Verify with go test -count=2 ./internal/store/, not just -count=1.

packages.spec: Issue 219: cancelled-context coverage for lease methods
packages.focus: internal/jobs/runner_test.go's fakeStore takes an unused context.Context on all three lease methods (RenewJobLeases, FailOrphanedJobs, ReleaseJobLeases), so nothing covers what RunLeases does when a cancelled context reaches one of those calls - and RunLeases suppresses exactly that case today (if the statement context's own Err() is non-nil, the renewal failure is not logged), silently and with a green suite. Give fakeStore a mode where the three lease methods honour context cancellation (return ctx.Err() when the context passed to them is done), and add a test asserting the intended behaviour of a cancelled stmtCtx - deciding explicitly, and saying so in the PR, whether the current silence is right at all, since with context.Background() in production (cmd/inventory/main.go) the guard can only ever fire for a caller that is already misusing the API, which arguably deserves a warning like any other renewal failure rather than silence. Do not change RunLeases' own loop-exit semantics: r.base.Done() is the loop's only correct exit (settled by PR #218's own fix, renaming the statement-level parameter to stmtCtx precisely so a future caller cannot reintroduce the signal-context bug) and review-go already confirmed the guard should not be changed to reference r.base - this issue is a missing-test gap around a guard that is already correct, not a behaviour change.

internal/migrate/check.go:50-51 prints a schema-mismatch hint - a single-file compose invocation to run migrations and bring the app back up - that is right for a plain clone but still starts Traefik on the Synology NAS variant (missing the docker-compose.nas.yml layer), asking for DSM's own port 80. Same category as #112 items 1 and 3, already fixed for internal/config's missing-.env error and the setup wizard's closing hint by PR #192 - read that fix first. Either stop naming a specific compose invocation in the message, matching #192's approach, or make the message itself state that the NAS variant needs the two-file form. The same text is quoted in docs/specs/18-operations-and-observability.md:134-135 - update it to match whatever the message ends up saying, carrying the same NAS caveat if the message keeps naming a command. No other file needs to change.

packages.spec: Issue 196: live Gemini call in the merge gate
packages.focus: internal/vision/live_test.go:98's TestLiveAnalyzeProductHonoursContract makes a real call to the Gemini API and runs as part of go test ./..., which is the merge gate - a transient 503/429 from Google turns an unrelated PR red, and the cure everyone reaches for (rerun it) is precisely the habit that later hides a genuine intermittent failure. #113 already fixed the identical test (this same TestLiveAnalyzeProductHonoursContract) in wave 2 with the provider-outage-skip pattern - read that fix (PR #199, commit 52203b7) before choosing here, since it already closes part of what this issue describes, and the remaining scope may be narrower than a fresh skip implementation: likely just the cost/merge-gate-exposure half (a build tag or GEMINI_LIVE_TEST=1 env var so go test ./... never reaches the test at all), not the outage-vs-contract-violation distinction, which #113 already handles correctly. Either gate this test behind a build tag or an env var such as GEMINI_LIVE_TEST=1 so go test ./... never reaches it, or t.Skip when the key is absent or the call answers a 5xx while keeping a contract violation inside a SUCCESSFUL response a hard failure - a blanket skip on any error is explicitly the wrong fix, since the test's whole purpose is the contract. CI is unaffected either way (it sets no GEMINI_API_KEY), and this project's own sessions already blank the key deliberately for the same reason. Say in the PR how you exercised both the outage and the contract-violation branches without waiting for a real outage.

scripts/tests/wellen-orchestrator.test.ps1 dot-sources every function above the Main flow marker, including Invoke-Wave's parallel (sequential: false) branch, but nothing exercises that branch's own polling loop - the one that tears each package's stack down the moment its own issue closes, in actual-close order rather than file order. Add a test that shadows Test-IssueClosed, Stop-PackageStack, Invoke-Package and Start-Sleep to fake a two-package wave where the second-listed package's fake issue closes before the first's, and assert the teardown order matches actual close order - on the order of 15 lines, well within this file's existing style. The test must actually catch these two concrete regressions: dropping the reassignment of the still-pending list after each poll cycle (spins the loop forever, since already-torn-down packages keep getting re-checked but the loop never shrinks or exits), and swapping the closed-issue branch so the still-pending list is added to on the closed condition instead of the open one (tears every package's stack down on every single poll cycle instead of once, when it actually closes). Do not change wellen-orchestrator.ps1 itself - this is a pure test addition against existing, correct behaviour.

packages.spec: Issue 211: compose_test.go reads unmounted root files
packages.focus: cmd/inventory/compose_test.go's repoFile helper reads root-level files - docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.nas.yml, docker-compose.e2e.yml, .gitignore, .dockerignore, scripts/backup - none of which docker-compose.override.yml mounts into the dev container, so a local docker compose run --rm app go test ./... verdicts against the image's last-built copy of those files, not the working tree. This is the same silent-staleness class the override file already documents for ./migrations and ./deploy, just never extended to cover what compose_test.go reads. Pick one of three shapes and say which and why in the PR: mount the specific files individually (narrow, but must be kept in step with whatever the test file grows to read next); mount ./scripts as a directory plus the compose files; or mount the project root read-only at a second path and have repoFile prefer it (broader blast radius). Whichever you choose, do NOT mount the project directory into the backup service itself - TestBackupServiceMountsOnlyWhatMayTravel deliberately asserts it never gets one, and that assertion must keep passing. The tests currently reading baked-in copies are TestBackupServiceMountsOnlyWhatMayTravel, TestNASVariantGivesBackupTheBindMountedUploads, TestBackupArchivesAreNotCommittable, TestBackupWritesUnderATemporaryNameAndRenames, TestBackupScriptIsPinnedToLFEndings, TestE2EBackupServiceMatchesTheProductionOne and TestE2EAppMountsTheUploadsTheRoundTripDestroys - verify all of them still pass, and still verify what they claim to, after your mount change. CI is unaffected (it builds fresh); this is a local-loop fix only, no production code.

serve() in cmd/inventory/main.go starts SIX background loops as bare go statements, and nothing asserts any of them is actually reached: go imageCache.RunSweeps(ctx) (line 300), go runStoreSweeps(ctx, db, ingestSweep) (line 393), go jobRunner.RunLeases(context.Background()) (line 338 - deliberately context.Background(), not ctx, per #218/#219; do not change that argument), go runGamificationRecompute(ctx, db) (line 394), go runWeeklyGamificationJobs(ctx, db) (line 395), and go runExpiryNotifications(ctx, notifier) (line 403). Verify this list of six against current main yourself before starting, since three of them (the two gamification loops and the notification loop) were added after this issue was filed and the issue's own text names only three. Deleting any one line keeps docker compose run --rm app go test ./... green, because each loop's own package tests call it directly rather than through serve(). The blast radius is largest for RunLeases: issue #121's whole fix is that line and nothing else, and losing it silently would reintroduce the pre-#121 behaviour (jobs from a force-removed instance pending for good) with a green suite and docs/specs/04-backend-api-conventions.md plus deploy/synology/README.md both still claiming the sweep runs for as long as the process serves - but the same untested-wiring gap applies equally to all six, expiry notifications included, so the fix must cover all six, not just the three the issue names. Give the six go statements a named home - a small startBackgroundLoops function, or a slice of func(context.Context) - that a test can invoke with a cancelled context and a fake store/cache/notifier, asserting each loop is entered. Do not change serve()'s listener-binding behaviour or any loop's own internal logic, and do not change RunLeases' context argument - this is wiring-level coverage only.

packages.spec: Issue 197: NAS update unguarded final prune
packages.focus: deploy/synology/update:199's maybe_prune (checks whether prune is zero, otherwise runs docker image prune -f) is the last thing all four of the script's exit paths do (lines 300, 327, 351, 444 - the comment above it says so deliberately), and the whole script runs under set -eu, so a transient docker image prune failure (another docker command holding a lock, an image that started being used between listing and removal, a plain daemon hiccup) turns a fully successful update into a non-zero exit - which on an unattended NAS update is exactly the signal that means something went wrong, do not walk away. This got worse when #124's wave-1 fix correctly routed all four exits through maybe_prune instead of two, doubling how many successful outcomes now end on this unguarded command. Guard it so cleanup cannot fail the update - check whether the script already has a warn-style helper and match it (die is the wrong one here by definition); simply swallowing the error would also technically work but a warning tells the operator the requested prune did not happen rather than staying silent about it. While in the file, check whether any other cleanup-shaped command sits unguarded on an exit path under set -eu and fix it the same way if so. No new flag, no rollback path - this is a guard on one already-correct cleanup step.

docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md:51 gives the E2E deployment gate as a single command, docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml run --rm e2e, and that command fails all 131 tests: the e2e service only declares depends_on: app, so traefik never starts, and the suite's BASE_URL pointing at traefik makes every request fail at DNS resolution before the browser suite does anything real. docker-compose.e2e.yml's own header comment already has the correct six-step sequence (build, migrate up, up -d, seed, run --rm e2e, down -v) - fix the spec table to carry that sequence or point at the one place that has it, with no second copy that can drift. #209 found a second, independent gap the same way: the suite is not idempotent (nothing resets between runs), so a second run against a still-up stack fails about 21 tests that look exactly like product bugs (a fresh POST of a barcode answering 409 instead of 201, observed live during wave 2's consolidation) - state the clean-database requirement where someone running the suite will actually read it, naming the consequence (roughly 21 failures with symptoms that look like real bugs) rather than only listing the down -v step as if it were tidiness. Also document the Git-Bash-on-Windows trap #195 records: the seed step needs MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, or MSYS rewrites the container path /fixtures/seed.sql into a host path and psql fails to find the file - worth one line since every session on this machine hits it. Close both #195 and #209 in this PR. Do NOT attempt #209's own optional item 4 (giving the e2e service a depends_on: traefik in docker-compose.e2e.yml) - #190 in wave 11 of this same plan is independently determining that file's actual per-worktree isolation behaviour, and a change here would land ahead of and could conflict with that investigation. Leave docker-compose.e2e.yml completely untouched; this package is documentation only, and no e2e/specs/*.js file needs to change.

packages.spec: Issue 228: specs 05 and 28 still describe js/review.js rendering
packages.focus: docs/specs/05-frontend-pwa-foundations.md:126-130 and docs/specs/28-batch-move-quick-create.md:13-14,20 both describe two screens as rendering through the shared js/review.js component: the ingestion review row (spec 06, web/static/js/pages/review.js) and the shopping-list resolution UI (spec 07, web/static/js/pages/shopping-list.js). Verify each file's own imports before touching either sentence, rather than assuming #228's own framing of which half is stale is correct: web/static/js/pages/review.js still imports ReviewList from ../review.js, so the ingestion-row half of the claim is accurate today and must be left alone in both specs; web/static/js/pages/shopping-list.js has no such import, so the shopping-list-resolution half is the one that is actually stale and needs fixing in both specs. Fix only that half, leave the ingestion-row sentence untouched in both files, and say in the PR which half you changed and why the other was left alone. Do not conflate this with the unrelated, already-fixed claim from wave 5's #154 item 4: that one was about specs 26 and 27 wrongly naming js/review.js as the trigger call site for openLocationField/openCategoryField (the tree-modal quick-create openers), a completely different component and files, already corrected and not part of this issue. Do not touch #154 item 6's three-review-screens wording in spec 28 - already verified resolved on main by an earlier round and unrelated. Documentation only, no code change, no test.

packages.spec: Issues 221, 227: tree-modal mutation tracking and refusal signalling
packages.focus: Two related gaps in web/static/js/tree-modal.js's mutual-exclusion and mutation-tracking logic added by #144 and #154 (PRs #222 and #220) - close both #221 and #227 in this PR. #221: pendingMutation is a single slot naming only the most recently started mutation, so when an earlier-started mutation (A) settles AFTER a later one (B) - plausible, since network responses are not ordered by request order - runMutation(B) finishes first, correctly nulls the slot since nothing superseded it, any requestClose() waiting on B sees the slot empty and finalizes, and A's still-in-flight create never makes it into the resolved createdIds with a late error landing in a dialog that is already gone - the exact failure #154 item 2 was filed to close, reintroduced for the reverse operand order. Track the SET of outstanding mutation attempts (a counter, or a Set of promises) rather than a single slot, and finalize only once that set is empty, so settle order stops mattering; e2e/specs/ingestion.spec.js's existing two-overlapping-creates test already holds two POSTs open via page.route and releases them in start order, so swapping that release order reproduces the drop and should become your regression test. #227: openTreeManager's dialogOpen guard refuses a second trigger instantly, but its two callers - openLocationField in web/static/js/location-options.js and openCategoryField in web/static/js/category-options.js - never check the outcome, so a refused click still falls through into a real fetchLocations or fetchCategories GET and a full option refresh, and a hiccup on that incidental request surfaces a spurious network-error banner for a click the app deliberately chose to ignore. Have openTreeManager report whether it actually opened (it already knows), and have both callers return early when it did not, before the fetch. While in the file, add the one-line invariant comment review-go asked for on requestClose's recursive settle-order re-check - it is correct, just dense enough to deserve it. No server code, no CLAUDE.md silent invariant - this is client-side bookkeeping and UI-refusal signalling only.

packages.spec: Issue 224: move form required attribute is untested
packages.focus: web/static/js/pages/products.js:642 added required to the move form's moveTarget select, alongside the same fix on splitQuantity and splitTarget, but e2e/specs/products.spec.js's new native-validation test (submitting the split form with an empty quantity and no target is blocked by native validation, not a silent no-op) only exercises the split form. Add the mirrored test for the move form: assert moveTarget's validity.valid is false directly after an empty submit. Assert validity.valid directly rather than checking for request absence alone - the move form has a pre-existing no-op-on-same-location guard in internal/store/batches.go's moveBatch that makes an empty-target submit hard to distinguish from a submit that reached the server and hit that guard, which is exactly why this needed its own test rather than reusing the split form's assertion style. No production code change - the fix already shipped and works, verified by review-go and review-docs across two rounds; this is coverage only.

Determine, with a real docker compose ... up (not only config), what an E2E run is actually named and isolated as in each invocation style this plan's own tooling uses: from a package worktree (which has its own COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME written into .env by Set-WorktreeEnvOverrides), from the main checkout, and from a scratch clone with no .env at all. docker-compose.e2e.yml pins name: inventory-e2e with a comment explaining why (without it the file would share the default inventory project with docker-compose.yml/override.yml and Compose would recreate containers by name across configs) - but a worktree's own COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME overrides a file's name:, confirmed on #140 with a single config call but never against a real up, so whether a package session running the E2E suite from inside its own worktree actually gets an isolated project per worktree, or still shares the literal inventory-e2e project, is still genuinely open. Make the answer deliberate rather than emergent: either give the E2E stack a real per-worktree project name on purpose, or establish plainly that it must stay the one shared project and that two worktrees may never run the E2E suite concurrently (today's de facto answer, enforced by nothing outside a sequential wave). Then correct docker-compose.e2e.yml's own name: comment, and the three documentation pointers that currently describe this as open: scripts/wellen-orchestrator.ps1's DOCKER CLEANUP header block, its Stop-PackageStack comment, and scripts/wellen-planen.md's Docker cleanup after a wave per-package paragraph. This is the only package in this plan touching docker-compose.e2e.yml - wave 10's #195/#209 package was told explicitly to leave that file alone so it could not land ahead of this investigation. No application code changes; this is Docker-configuration and documentation only.
